name: array-axes-slicing
title: 1D half-open slices and 2D axis reductions
description: Left panel shows 1D array a = [10, 20, 30, 40, 50] with 0-based indices 0..4 and negative indices -5..-1, where half-open a[1:4] returns [20, 30, 40] (4 excluded) and a[::2] returns [10, 30, 50]. Right panel shows a (2, 3) grid [[1, 2, 3], [10, 20, 30]] where axis=0 sums down rows to [11, 22, 33] and axis=1 sums across columns to [6, 60].

name: array-views
title: Slice view (shared memory) versus .copy()
description: From original = [10, 20, 30, 40], view = original[:2] followed by view[0] = 99 mutates the shared buffer to [99, 20, 30, 40], whereas sep = original[:2].copy() followed by sep[0] = -5 writes [-5, 20] in a new buffer and leaves original unchanged.

name: python-environments
title: One project environment for both kernel and shell
description: Pick one solver per project (uv with uv.lock, pip + venv, or conda/mamba for Python + C/GPU) to build an isolated .venv/bin/python used by both the Python PhD (locked) Jupyter kernel and an activated shell, whereas an unactivated shell bypasses .venv and raises ModuleNotFoundError.

name: shared-mask
title: One shared mask preserves row alignment
description: Applying one shared boolean mask valid = [T, F, F, T] keeps rows 0 and 3 aligned across dist, vel, and sigma, whereas separate per-column masks both return shape (3,) and silently pair row 2's velocity with row 1's sigma.

name: broadcasting
title: Broadcasting (M, 1) * (N,) to (M, N)
description: Column vector h0_grid[:, None] of shape (201, 1) multiplies distance[valid] of shape (395,) plus 300 to form v_model of shape (201, 395), followed by .sum(axis=1) returning chi2 of shape (201,).

name: catalogue-selection
title: Data quality versus selection threshold
description: From 400 raw rows, data-quality filtering removes 5 invalid rows to leave 395 valid rows, and threshold cut m < 16.5 selects 262 rows (leaving 133 faint valid rows) for comparison on shared bins.

name: fits-vs-ecsv
title: Text ECSV versus binary FITS
description: ECSV pairs a #-commented YAML header (units and metadata) with plain-text rows; FITS pairs Primary HDU 0 with Binary Table HDU 1 storing column units and short <=8-character header cards.

name: nyquist-aliasing
title: Nyquist folding at fs = 512 Hz
description: With 256 Hz Nyquist limit, a 40 Hz tone stays resolved in [0, 256 Hz], whereas a 300 Hz tone (256 + 44 Hz) folds across 256 Hz to a 212 Hz alias (512 - 300 Hz).

name: git-zones-lifecycle
title: Git zones and commands
description: Four zones from left to right — Working tree (saved files), Staging index (next snapshot), Local .git (commits), and Remote (origin) — connected by git add, git commit, git push, restore --staged, reset --soft, git fetch, and git clone or git pull.

name: git-states
title: git commit records the staged snapshot
description: Staging v1 (1 test) with git add and then editing disk to v2 (2 tests) without restaging means git commit records Commit: v1 (1 test only) while v2 stays unstaged.

name: git-merge-types
title: Fast-forward merge versus three-way merge
description: Top panel shows a fast-forward merge sliding main forward from C1 to C2 along linear history; bottom panel shows diverged commits A (main) and B (feature) joining in two-parent merge commit M.

name: git-branches
title: Competing edits pause for conflict resolution
description: From base C, branch A ('in degrees') and branch B ('shortest arc') edit the same line, pausing at a conflict until resolved and committed together as M ('degrees + shortest arc').

name: git-undo-vs-revert
title: Private soft reset versus shared forward revert
description: Top panel shows git reset --soft HEAD~1 rewinding a private unpushed branch from C2 back to C1 while keeping edits staged; bottom panel shows git revert HEAD keeping pushed mistake C2 in history and adding C3 to revert it safely.

name: git-remotes
title: Syncing a local clone with a remote
description: git clone makes the initial local copy; git fetch updates tracking ref origin/main from remote main; merge or pull integrates into the local branch; git push uploads local commits to remote main.

name: git-clone-fork-pr
title: Group repository versus open-source Fork and Pull Request
description: Top panel shows a group repository with write access (clone origin, push branch, open PR into main); bottom panel shows an external repository without write access (Fork upstream to personal origin, clone, push to origin, open PR to upstream, and fetch upstream).

name: agent-architecture
title: Agent client, tools and model host
description: On your workstation, the agent client (Claude Code, Codex, or Cline) mediates approvals for the file tool and optional OS-sandboxed terminal against workspace files, while exchanging context and proposals with an API or local LLM host.

name: agent-review-loop
title: Human-controlled agent verification loop
description: Eight-step loop between YOU and AGENT: 1 Task and expectations, 2 Propose plan, 3 Derive test cases, 4 Draft test file, 5 Commit tests, 6 Repair code (authorised), 7 Rerun and diff (with steer feedback), and 8 Commit and AI_USE.md.
